posts.body_html: Obviously it was warm, but what sort of temperatures did you experience there at this time of year?
posts.body_text: Obviously it was warm, but what sort of temperatures did you experience there at this time of year?

posts.body_html:
There's over a 1000 photos from this trip, so stay tuned, you haven't seen anything yet, haha

Oh, missed your question about the temperature....it was 85F (29C) at around 8:30 in the morning, and it averaged about 92 F (33C) during the day. Some days, it was in the 100's (38C) Let me add that the humidity was probably 90+ percent the whole time, and you have to be very tough to stay out in the full sun under these conditions. It's hard to picture just how savage it is out there, but heat exhaustion kicks in very quickly. Our shirts were constantly soaked in sweat, and if you stay outside for more 6 hours straight without hydrating, you'll likely pass out. I'm part Taiwanese, so my genes can handle this weather, but Axel and Damon couldn't stay out for as long as I could (or maybe I'm just crazier about the plants than they are )
So so so so epic.. Thanks for posting photos..

posts.body_html:
I just looked at the stream of your photos from Bob Hanrahan's property and it brought back many memories.  I first visited his property in 1984- before the house was built.  My last visit was in 2006.  Quite a change- always more plants than the previous visit.  Bob had definitely learned to farm the plants to the max.  As he said to me, he wanted to be the second largest producer of CP seed, the first being Mother Nature.
We often joked that he knowingly went out and bought 40 acres of swampland, the only condition being that Sarracenia was present.  As one can see, they are doing well.  I'm glad that Mike and Kate are taking excellent care of things and carrying forth with Bob's legacy.
